findings.location: Section 1 defect table (row 'No graceful shutdown') and Section 2D ('The shutdown path is an accident'); Section 8 Phase 2 module spec
findings.finding: The draft's 'never reliable' audit omits the crash half of defect D6. The current unit ships unitConfig ConditionUser only -- NixOS user services default Restart=no -- so a panicked agent stays dead until the next reboot, taking the host's telemetry with it. The draft covers the SIGTERM/will-discard trap thoroughly, but nowhere states that nothing restarts the process today (grep of the draft: 'Restart=no', 'crashed', 'watchdog' all zero hits); Section 5B and Phase 2 list Restart=on-failure as new-module config without ever flagging it as closing a live gap. The interim also carries a named hardening mechanism the draft drops entirely: WatchdogSec via sd_notify, ESPHome's reboot_timeout analogue -- reboot the agent after 15 minutes without a healthy loop. Given the research query is literally 'never reliable', a crash that ends telemetry until reboot is a third leg of the complaint alongside the two MQTT bugs.
findings.evidence: interim-report-mqtt-lifecycle-supervisor-spec, defect D6: 'ha-agent.nix:104-106 defines systemd.user.services.ha-linux-agent.unitConfig = { ConditionUser = "io"; } and nothing else -- NixOS user services default Restart=no, so a crashed agent stays dead until reboot... systemd: Restart=on-failure, RestartSec=5s, plus WatchdogSec= via sd_notify (ESPHome's reboot_timeout analogue: reboot the agent after 15 min without a healthy loop) -- at minimum Restart=on-failure so a panic doesn't kill the host's telemetry until the next boot.'
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to Section 2D (or a row in the Section 1 table) stating that the current user unit carries no restart policy at all -- user services default Restart=no -- so an agent crash today means no telemetry until the next reboot; and add the WatchdogSec/sd_notify healthy-loop watchdog (15 min, ESPHome's reboot_timeout analogue) to the Phase 1 or Phase 2 module spec alongside Restart=on-failure, framed as closing the crash leg of 'never reliable'.

findings.location: Section 2D final sentence ('add --decommission, publishing zero-length payloads to every owned topic, HA's official removal semantic') and Section 8 Phase 1 ('--decommission zero-payload mode')
findings.finding: A developed mechanism is compressed to a bare mention. The interim's D7 is the ghost-entity design: retained discovery configs survive HA restarts and resurrect removed entities because the v3.1.1 path forecloses message expiry (ESPHome ships clean-mqtt for exactly this problem) -- plus a four-part spec: derive the topic list from the same descriptors used for discovery 'so the two can never drift'; clear state/availability FIRST and configs LAST (mirroring Homie's state-first ordering rule); and emit opportunistically when the configured sensor/command set differs from the last published set (persisted in /var/lib/ha-linux-agent/last-discovery.json), clearing removed topics on next start. The draft's one clause recovers none of this; the drift-prevention and ordering rules are the difference between a decommission that works and one that leaves half-cleaned entities resurrecting.
findings.evidence: interim-report-mqtt-lifecycle-supervisor-spec, D7 spec: 'publishes zero-length payloads to every discovery config topic it owns, then to the state and availability topics (order: state/availability first, configs last, mirroring Homie's state-first rule); derive the topic list from the same descriptors used for discovery so the two can never drift. Also emit it opportunistically: if the configured sensor/command set differs from the last published set (persisted in e.g. /var/lib/ha-linux-agent/last-discovery.json), clear the removed topics on next start.' Rationale: 'A host decommissioned, or sensors removed from its config, leave retained discovery configs that resurrect on every HA restart (ESPHome ships clean-mqtt for exactly this).'
findings.suggested_fix: Expand the Section 2D sentence to carry the design: topic list derived from the same descriptors as discovery (cannot drift), state/availability-first then configs-last ordering per Homie, the ghost-resurrection rationale (retained configs survive HA restarts, no v3.1.1 message expiry to age them), and the opportunistic last-discovery.json diff that clears removed topics on config change at next start.

findings.location: Section 5D ('One residual risk is named rather than hedged... no notification daemon (mako, dunst, swaync) ships anywhere in the fleet... the kiosks' real last mile is the customer-display VFD (vacuum-fluorescent display) overlay [[interim-report-adopt-vs-build-honest-verdict]]')
findings.finding: Two provenance failures on the paragraph the synthesizer itself flagged as single-sourced. (1) Misattributed citation: the notification-daemon absence (no mako/dunst/swaync in jupiter-os) is NOT in the cited adopt-vs-build note -- it is fleet-service-model's Open question 1 plus the step-8 gap-wave update; a revisor following the citation finds nothing (verified: only fleet-service-model contains mako/dunst among the interim notes). (2) Unanchored claim: 'the customer-display VFD overlay' appears in zero vault notes -- searches for 'VFD' and 'vacuum-fluorescent' return nothing; the phrasing exists only in the run's comparisons.md step-8 update, so the paragraph's most concrete detail cites a note that never says it. (3) Over-claimed risk shape: the cross-locus reconciliation explicitly holds that notify.mqtt solves only the transport-into-the-agent leg; the session-bus last mile still needs the Environment block, the residual 'stands for hosts with desktops', and the Environment block is 'conditional on a future desktop host class'. The draft's 'dissolves most of it' / 'retires the risk outright' flattens this into a kiosk-only dead-code story -- and the Phase 2 exit criterion ('the notification live test on amalthea retires the fleet section's residual risk') inherits the problem: with no notification daemon on the kiosks, a delivery test as scoped cannot exercise the last mile it is meant to retire. The interim's own prescription is a busctl check for an org.freedesktop.Notifications owner first.
findings.evidence: interim-report-fleet-service-model-by-host-class, Open question 1: 'greps found no mako/dunst package in jupiter-os; notifications may already be dead code on every host, which would make the whole session-bus Environment block unnecessary rather than merely untested. Worth one live busctl check on amalthea before the module rewrite.' Confidence field: 'the residual 20-25% is whether notifications-on-kiosks (the one feature that genuinely wants io's session bus) behaves identically when reached from a system service -- untested on live hardware.' Cross-locus tension 5 (research/runs/linux-agent-jupiteros-fleet-15537b/comparisons.md): 'notify.mqtt fixes the transport into the agent... the agent's last mile -- calling org.freedesktop.Notifications on the session bus -- still needs the Environment block... the residual risk stands for hosts with desktops, and vanishes for headless hosts where the notification backend should simply not enable.' Vault searches for 'VFD'/'vacuum-fluorescent': zero hits.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-anchor the Section 5D paragraph: attribute the daemon-absence to [[interim-report-fleet-service-model-by-host-class]] (open question 1) and the VFD-overlay last-mile to the step-8 corpus-critic update (or verify the customer-display-is-a-VFD claim against jupiter-os before shipping it); restate the risk as conditional -- dead code on today's kiosks, standing for any future desktop host class, with the Environment block conditional likewise -- and rescope the amalthea verification item to the interim's actual prescription: a busctl check for an org.freedesktop.Notifications owner on the kiosk before any delivery test can mean anything.

findings.location: Section 5C SMART bullet ('the hook receives the full event context via SMARTD_MESSAGE/... and hands it to the agent, which never touches the ioctl'); Section 6 SMART/NVMe paragraph
findings.finding: The draft carries the smartd hook's inputs and the blocking caveat but drops the channel design -- HOW a root-owned smartd event reaches an unprivileged agent, which IS the zero-capability claim's mechanism. The interim specifies two concrete hand-off designs: the hook (a root-owned script, the smartd-warning.d convention, wired via a jupiter.storage.smartMonitoring.hook option or a fixed /usr/share/smartmontools/smartd_warning.d/ entry) either (a) drops a JSON line into /var/lib/ha-linux-agent/smartd/ for the agent to pick up, or (b) publishes directly to the agent's MQTT user as a low-privilege user. Without this, 'hands it to the agent' is a gesture at the mechanism the depth budget was spent on. Also dropped: europa's audited disk inventory (Marvell 88SE9230 SATA HBA, WD 18TB drives plus one OS SSD, all SATA, no NVMe) -- which shows even the rejected capability alternative would be CAP_SYS_RAWIO-only on this fleet, not the 'new root' CAP_SYS_ADMIN the Scrutiny quote warns about.
findings.evidence: interim-report-headless-privilege-ladder, SMART synthesis: 'the exec hook (a tiny root-owned script, the smartd-warning.d convention) writes into a world-writable spool or publishes straight to MQTT as a low-priv user, and the agent picks it up... add a jupiter.storage.smartMonitoring.hook option (or a fixed /usr/share/smartmontools/smartd_warning.d/ entry) that either (a) drops a JSON line into /var/lib/ha-linux-agent/smartd/ for the agent to pick up, or (b) publishes directly to the ha-linux-agent MQTT user.' Ground truth: 'its SATA HBA (Marvell 88SE9230) and WD 18TB drives + one OS SSD are all SATA (no NVMe)'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to Section 5C's SMART bullet naming the two hand-off designs (spool file the agent reads vs direct MQTT publish as a low-privilege user) and the NixOS surface (smartd_warning.d entry / jupiter.storage.smartMonitoring.hook option); optionally scope the capability-rejection to the fleet's actual disks by noting europa's audited all-SATA inventory, so the rejected CAP_SYS_ADMIN grant is a fortiori unnecessary on this hardware.

findings.location: Section 5B ('The system-service design') and Section 5C summed paragraph ('the existing polkit rule pattern for the specific units the launcher may start/stop')
findings.finding: Two named mechanisms that make the one-unit design work are gestured at without their content. (1) Why not a dynamic or dedicated system user: the interim eliminates DynamicUser= on upstream authority -- 'currently incompatible with D-Bus policies, thus a service using this option may currently not allocate a D-Bus service name (note that this does not affect calling into other D-Bus services)' -- and it implies ProtectSystem=strict/ProtectHome=read-only, 'which would block the agent's sysfs/probe surface'. Without this elimination the draft's User=io choice reads as preference rather than the last shape standing. (2) Why the existing polkit rules survive unchanged: they key on subject.user == 'io', which a User=io system service satisfies, so the launcher's scope=system commands keep working identically with zero new grants. The draft says the pattern survives but not the mechanism that guarantees it.
findings.evidence: interim-report-fleet-service-model-by-host-class: systemd.exec quote (DynamicUser D-Bus service-name incompatibility, calling-into-buses still works, ProtectSystem=strict implication); and 'its scope = "system" path is polkit-gated for io today and would keep working identically under a system service running as io -- the polkit rules key on subject.user == "io", which a User=io system service satisfies.'
findings.suggested_fix: Add two sentences to Section 5B: DynamicUser= is ruled out because it cannot allocate a D-Bus service name and implies ProtectSystem=strict (blocking the sysfs/probe surface), so a static User=io is the canonical minimal shape; and the existing polkitUnitRule grants key on subject.user == 'io', which a User=io system service satisfies unchanged -- the launcher's system-scope commands transfer with zero new grants.

findings.location: Section 2A (PR #1052 discussion), Section 2 boundary judgement 2 ('0.24.0 is not v3.1.1-locked'), Section 8 Forward-looking ('the v5 module already ships inside the pinned version')
findings.finding: Two verification details that answer the argument's hardest questions are dropped. (1) Why ConnAck specifically: 0.24.0's Event enum has exactly two variants (Incoming/Outgoing) -- no Reconnect variant exists in the pinned version, so 'a second CONNACK is the only reconnect signal the pinned version offers'. The draft asserts the ConnAck-driven design as a structural choice without this clinching enumeration; the rumqttc-fitness committed position makes the implication explicit -- no signal event will arrive in the pinned version, making the raw ConnAck match mandatory. (2) The v5-module claim that Section 8 leans on for the future message-expiry cure is backed by a reachability analysis the draft omits: the single unimplemented!() in v5/state.rs:214 sits on request variants (PubComp/SubAck/UnsubAck/PingResp) the public client never sends -- unreachable from agent code -- i.e. the v5 module is not a stubbed half-implementation. A sceptical reader of Section 8's 'module switch away' has exactly this question pre-answered in the interim.
findings.evidence: interim-report-rumqttc-dependency-fitness: 'Event has exactly two variants -- "pub enum Event { Incoming(Incoming), Outgoing(Outgoing), }" -- no Reconnect variant in 0.24.0. poll() yields Event::Incoming(Packet::ConnAck) on every connect, so a second CONNACK is the only reconnect signal the pinned version offers.' And: 'The single unimplemented!() in v5/state.rs:214 sits on request variants (PubComp/SubAck/UnsubAck/PingResp) the public client never sends -- unreachable from agent code.'
findings.suggested_fix: In Section 2A or 2D, add the enum fact: 0.24.0's Event exposes only Incoming/Outgoing -- no Reconnect variant -- so the raw ConnAck match is not a workaround but the only hook the pinned version offers (and PR #1052's signal event will not arrive in it regardless). In boundary judgement 2 or Section 8, add the unimplemented!()-reachability note (the one stub sits on request variants the public client never sends) so 'v5 is a module switch away' carries its verification.

findings.finding: The live proof on callisto has two halves -- what worked (match-rule subscription: Subscribe() plus a JobRemoved signal delivered to unprivileged io) and what failed (busctl --system monitor, the BecomeMonitor eavesdropping API, is polkit-denied for io). The draft carries only the success half. The denial is a real implementation trap: BecomeMonitor is the more obvious observability API, and the interim's design caveat is explicit -- the agent must use match-rule subscription (zbus receive_signal / MessageStream with a match), never BecomeMonitor.
findings.evidence: interim-report-headless-privilege-ladder, live ground truth from callisto: '(1) busctl --system monitor (BecomeMonitor) is polkit-denied for io -- but that is only the eavesdropping API. (2) The normal match-rule subscription works unprivileged: mgr.Subscribe() succeeded as io, and a JobRemoved signal for logrotate.service... was delivered to an unprivileged subscriber.' Design caveat: 'the agent must use match-rule subscription (zbus receive_signal / MessageStream with a match), never BecomeMonitor.'
findings.suggested_fix: Add one clause to the unit-health bullet: the naive alternative -- BecomeMonitor (busctl --system monitor) -- was tried live on callisto and polkit-denied for io, so the design commits to match-rule subscription (zbus receive_signal/MessageStream with a match rule) specifically.

findings.finding: Both paragraphs the synthesizer flagged as two-sentence thin have interim substance the draft does not use. Mesh: the agent's backend-headscale already shells out to `tailscale status --json` today (the audited mechanism -- the verification work is verify-and-tolerance of an existing channel, not new parsing), and callisto is the audited mesh hub (headscale-target and tunnel duty among its service inventory). Remote reboot: the draft asserts 'non-idempotent commands are exactly the class a replayed stale message would damage' as settled; the interim left precisely this as an open question -- whether any launcher-style command semantics in this fleet are non-idempotent, noting that if none are, the clean_session question becomes lower-stakes than argued. The feature entry should name the idempotency audit as the concrete next step rather than treating the hazard as established.
findings.evidence: interim-report-headless-privilege-ladder, ground truth: 'backend-headscale shells to `tailscale status --json`' and 'callisto... runs mqtt (the broker), postgres, headscale-target, syncthing-hub (europa), arcade, model-router...' ; interim-report-mqtt-lifecycle-supervisor-spec, open questions: 'Whether any launcher-style command semantics in this fleet are non-idempotent (reboot/power commands) -- if none are, the clean_session question becomes lower-stakes than argued.'
findings.suggested_fix: Mesh paragraph: state that backend-headscale's current mechanism is the `tailscale status --json` shell-out (audited), so the ipnstate-schema work is verification and version-tolerance of an existing channel, running on the host that is the fleet's mesh hub. Reboot paragraph: replace the asserted hazard with the interim's open question -- an idempotency audit of the fleet's command handlers is the named next step, and its outcome calibrates the clean_session argument's stakes.

findings.location: Section 5C ZFS bullet ('plus a zedlet as the push channel: ZED... publishes *into* the agent's channel; services.zfs.zed.settings renders the configuration NixOS already ships')
findings.finding: The zed bridge's concrete mechanics are compressed away: zedlet registration is filename-prefix-based ('the prefix all matches all zevents') with zevents arriving as ZEVENT_-prefixed environment variables -- the exact parallel to the SMARTD_* surface the SMART bullet does carry; zedlets must be root-owned with no group/other write; and the deployment-cost fact that zfs-zed.service ships inside the zfs package and is wanted by zfs.target unconditionally when ZFS is enabled, with stock zedlets (statechange-notify.sh and siblings) already installed via environment.etc -- jupiterOS needs to define no unit for ZED, only to populate zed.rc and drop one custom zedlet.
findings.evidence: interim-report-headless-privilege-ladder, zed(8)/zfs.nix synthesis: 'zedlet matching is filename-prefix-based ("the prefix all matches all zevents"), zevent nvpars arrive as ZEVENT_-prefixed environment variables, and -- decisive for the privilege design -- "The ZED requires root privileges" and "ZEDLETs must be owned by root... must not have write permissions for group or other"... the zfs-zed.service unit ships inside the zfs package (systemd.packages = [ cfgZfs.package ]) and is wanted by zfs.target unconditionally when ZFS is enabled -- jupiterOS does not need to define any unit for ZED, only to populate zed.rc and drop a custom zedlet.'
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the ZFS bullet: zevents arrive as ZEVENT_-prefixed environment variables (the same spool/push trick as the smartd SMARTD_* hook), zedlet registration is filename-prefix-based with root-owned no-group-write zedlets, and no new unit is needed -- zfs-zed.service is already wanted by zfs.target on ZFS hosts; only zed.rc values plus one custom zedlet.

findings.location: Section 7 (ladder preamble and step 5); Section 8 Phase 0

Also dropped: the house style the ladder extends -- the eight existing tests are 'named regression guards with explanatory comment blocks (Regression guard: ... See commit e28ca83)', which is what the five defect-named tests are designed to match.

Test inventory: 'All 8 are pure #[test]s on shape/parsing functions, all written as named regression guards with explanatory comment blocks ("Regression guard: ... See commit e28ca83") -- that style is the house style to match.'
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to Section 7 (around the ladder preamble or step 5): the harness needs zero new flake ingredients -- mosquitto already in the devShell, dbus already in commonArgs buildInputs, crane attributes passing straight through so the broker rides nativeBuildInputs -- and note the five defect-named tests follow the repo's existing regression-guard comment style (the See-commit-e28ca83 pattern).

findings.location: Section 1 privilege-workaround paragraph; Section 5C backlight bullet; Section 8 Phase 2 ('the udev GROUP=video rule plus io-in-video for backlight writes')
findings.finding: The interim's prescriptive section flags a write-path detail the draft misses: kiosks run the hardware backend's backlight disabled -- their brightness entity is the launcher's screen-power light profile (backlight = ""), whose writes go through the same raw sysfs path. So the udev GROUP=video fix must cover the LAUNCHER backend's write path too (or its own capability), not only the backend-hardware write_sys_file surface the Section 1 audit names. A reader fixing 'the hardware backend's sysfs writes' would fix the path the kiosks do not actually use.
findings.evidence: interim-report-fleet-service-model-by-host-class, prescriptive specificity item 4: 'kiosks keep NO capabilities and simply lose write-governor/backlight -- kiosks already run backlight = false and their brightness goes through the launcher light profile, which must then ALSO move to a udev GROUP="video" + users.users.io.extraGroups = [ "video" ] fix or its own capability.' Ground truth: the launcher screen-power profile with backlight = "" (one dimmable HA light).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a clause to Section 5C's backlight bullet or Phase 2: the kiosks' brightness entity is the launcher's light profile (the hardware backend's backlight is disabled on kiosks), so the udev GROUP=video + io-in-video fix must be written against the launcher backend's write path -- the deployed consumer of the sysfs writes is the launcher profile, not backend-hardware.

findings.location: Section 3 'The identity and notification bars' paragraph ('no Linux agent implements the round-trip anywhere')
findings.finding: The absolute claim's one Linux-side counter-instance is handled in the transport paragraph but absent where the claim is made: halinuxcompanion implements mobile_app with an HTTP server for the notify round-trip -- a 90-star Python project whose own to-do is moving sensors to MQTT because the native API leaves them 'stuck' offline (the LWT problem). The steel-man of 'no round-trip anywhere' is exactly this project -- native-API, Linux, round-trip-shaped -- and its documented weaknesses (90 stars, self-planned MQTT migration) are what close it. Under the advocate register, the strongest counter-case belongs where the claim is asserted.
findings.evidence: interim-report-adopt-vs-build-honest-verdict, evidence synthesis: 'The only Linux-side implementations of the action round-trip are: (a) native-API agents (HASS.Agent is Windows-only; halinuxcompanion implements mobile_app with an HTTP server for the notify round-trip but is a 90-star Python project that itself lists "Move sensors to MQTT" as a to-do because "the limitations of the API" leave sensors "stuck" when the host goes offline -- the LWT problem), or (b) an MQTT agent inventing its own action vocabulary (buttons/selects per notification, automations listening on command topics).'
findings.suggested_fix: In the notifications paragraph, qualify the absolute claim with its strongest instance: halinuxcompanion is the one Linux agent with a native-API notify round-trip (an HTTP server for the mobile_app contract), and it is a 90-star project whose own roadmap moves sensors to MQTT because the native API strands them offline -- the exception that measures how small the MQTT-only sacrifice is.

structural_notes: No interim note is completely ignored -- all six are cited and substantially used. rumqttc-dependency-fitness and adopt-vs-build-honest-verdict are the best-carried; fleet-service-model-by-host-class is the one whose open-questions and prescriptive-specificity sections are most under-carried (findings depth-03, depth-05, and depth-11 all trace to it, including its own flagged 20-25% residual which the draft cites to the wrong note).

Several Section 5D/2C facts originate in the step-8 gap-wave updates recorded in research/runs/linux-agent-jupiteros-fleet-15537b/comparisons.md (the ~25-entity measurement, the mako/dunst/swaync finding, the 'customer-display VFD overlay' phrasing, the D9 recalibration). These are binding for the draft but have no vault-note citation target -- the patcher needs a citation path for them (cite the corpus-critic artifact or the underlying corpus notes), or the gap-fetch wave (step 13) should land them as proper sources. The 'VFD' detail in particular is currently unverifiable against any note in the vault.

The draft's Section 2C D9 recalibration (default 1000 never binds at ~25 entities; $SYS check; persistence true as the load-bearing half) correctly follows the step-8 binding update over the mqtt-spec interim's original 8192/4xR sizing -- no finding raised there.
